A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the differences in the amount and allocation of wood production between trees with a large crown and trees with a small crown are not related to the concentrations of IAA, amino acids and nitrogen in the differentiating xylems, the cambium and the cambial region, respectively, but rather to the amount of IAA and sucrose in the cambial tissues.
the growth of the stem is not directly related with the concentration of sucrose, indole-3acetic acid (IA A), nitrogen and amino acids, but with the activity of the cells.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the cambium is a highly dynamic system, which is capable of adjusting the amount of wood produced in response to changes in the environment.
the concentration of carbohydrates and IAA in cambial region is not directly related with annual ring width.
